title: Grading pinto bean products for sale; quality, impurities, and weight loss
excerpt: Guide to grading pinto beans for sale: the impact of harvesting conditions on seed visual quality, commercial standards, and post-harvest marketing channels
content_html:
Target market classification of beans and the importance of seed appearance

Pinto beans are one of the important cooking legumes, and their sales value is directly linked to the visual quality of the seed. Buyers pay special attention to color uniformity, glossiness, size consistency, and the absence of staining or visual defects before making a decision.

Academic source Confirms that the appearance of dry bean seeds has a direct impact on selling price, and buyers pay special attention to visual quality. This finding also applies to food-grade pinto beans, although official Iranian grading standards are not presented in available sources.

The impact of harvesting conditions on visual quality and color change

Weather conditions at harvest play a decisive role in maintaining the visual quality of bean seeds. Rainfall during harvest can cause color change in the seeds, and this effect is more noticeable in white-colored varieties.

Academic source Notes that rainfall during harvest causes color change in bean seeds, especially in white varieties. This observation is based on Missouri conditions, and generalizing it to Iran's climate requires review by agricultural experts.

Therefore, planning the timing of harvest and avoiding exposing the crop to rainfall after physiological maturity is considered an important measure to preserve the desirable appearance of seeds and their market value.

Quality standards and grading based on defects

Dry beans are classified into different commercial classes, and each class has its own specific visual characteristics. Understanding this classification helps the producer know which segment of the market their product belongs to and what quality specifications are required.

Academic source Explains that dry beans are classified into various commercial classes, each with specific visual features. This classification pertains to the USDA standard of the United States and has no official Iranian equivalent.

Quality classCharacteristicMarketing channel
Food qualityHas desirable appearance and color uniformityDirect sale to consumers or food industries
Targeted food qualityHas special quality specifications in demand by a specific buyerPre-harvest contract sale
Non-edibleDoes not meet food-grade standardsSale as animal feed

Some buyers only accept products that meet food-grade (food grade) standards. In such cases, the required quality specifications must be obtained from the buyer prior to product deliveryAcademic source.

Dry beans that do not meet food-grade standards are typically sold as animal feedAcademic source. This marketing channel allows the producer to avoid waste even when the product does not have a suitable appearance for food sale.

Post-harvest marketing channels

After harvest, the producer can use various options for selling depending on product quality and market conditions. Direct marketing to small food processors has been a successful experience for some producers.

It is recommended that a bean sales contract be concluded before planting to prevent stockpiling the product without a guaranteed market. National promotional and extension organizations can also assist in identifying potential buyersAcademic source.

In general, early identification of the target market, obtaining information about the quality specifications in demand by buyers, and sorting the product by quality grades are key factors in achieving a fair price for produced pinto beans.
